topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Engineering Students

sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 'Moving Window' Concept (1 minute)
lecture_lines: Convolution starts with a local neighborhood.
Imagine a sliding window over pixels.
This window computes a local weighted average.
It smooths or highlights specific image features.
This process is the discrete convolution.

sections.title: The Mathematical Mechanism (1.5 minutes)
lecture_lines: Convolution is element-wise multiplication and summation.
We flip the kernel for proper filtering.
The kernel slides across the entire image.
animations: Display two arrays, Data (color: #FFFFFF) and Kernel (color: #FFFF00) using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/photograph.svg] to represent the input structure.

Visualize the sliding operation and element-wise summation as a single output value (color: #00FF00) and capture the result using a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg].

sections.title: Kernel Personalities: Shaping Data (1.5 minutes)
lecture_lines: Different kernels change the image appearance.
Edge detection kernels highlight rapid differences.
animations: Display an identity kernel with a center 1 (color: #FFFFFF) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg].

Transition to an edge detection kernel with surrounding negative values (color: #FF4500) [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/photograph.svg].

sections.title: Real-World Application: Convolutional Neural Networks (1 minute)
lecture_lines: CNNs treat kernels as learnable parameters.
Layers learn filters for specific shapes.
AI uses these to detect complex objects.
